OBJECTIVES
This lesson introduces you to exponents and square roots.
INTRODUCTIONM
Even though exponents and square roots are not normally used every day, they provide a convenient way to express some numbers.
For example, finding the area of squares and circles uses exponents.
If you know the area, the side of a square and the radius of a circle can be found by using square roots.
Also, exponents are used to express very large or small numbers. 1,000,000,000,000 = 10 0.0000000000001 = 10

Let's discuss a few more facts about exponents.Power of 1 Power of 0 Negative Bases Negative Exponents
Power of 1: Any number to the power of 1 is equal to that number, or the base number.
A base number with an exponent of 1 is not multiplied by itself at all.
Power of 0 : Any number to the power of 0 is equal to 1.
Note that 0 to the 0 power is undefined....................
Negative Bases: Numbers with negative bases produce a positive number if the exponent is even and a negative number if the exponent is odd....
It is like multiplying signed numbers, a negative times a negative is a positive and a positive times a negative is a negative.
Negative Exponents Numbers with negative exponents produce the multiplication inverse or reciprocal of the number.
All you have to do is place the number in the denominator and a 1 as the numerator and change the exponent sign to positive.

DISCUSSION
The square root of a number is a number which when multiplied by itself gives the original number.
The symbol for the square root is and it is called a radical sign...
An alternate radical sign uses the number 2 to indicate a square root.
When a number appears under the radical sign, it means that you are to find a number which can be multiplied by itself to give the original number.
For example, the square root of 25 is 5.

SQUARE ROOT OF 36 - To find the square root of 36 you must find a number that when multiplied by itself equals the original number, 36.
Up to this point, the square root of numbers were easily calculated.
However, finding the square root of 2835 is not as easy!...
One way to solve for these difficult problems is to use a technique of modified division.
You first separate the number into groups of two starting at the decimal point.
Here are some additional examples showing the groups of two.
How would you group this number to find the square root?
To group the original number, start at the decimal point and go to the right and left.

Let's find the square root of 2835. The number has been grouped so we can start dividing.
Starting with the first group, find a number that when multiplied by itself will give an answer close but not larger than the first group.
Notice in the example that 5 is the largest number. Four squared equals 16 which is not close enough to 28. Six squared equals 36 which is too large..
Now, bring down the next group. Never bring down a single number. This is your new dividend.
Double the quotient, this is your new divisor, and place it to the left of your new dividend.
Ignore the last digit in the new dividend, the 5 in 335, find out how many times the new divisor, 10, will go into the new dividend, 33.
Now, place the result in the quotient and on the end of the new divisor, 10.
Multiply 3 times 103 and place the result under 335 (include the five in the dividend.) Subtract like you would do if dividing.
At this point you have found the approximate square root of 2835. However, 53 times 53 equals 2809 which is not close enough to 2835.
So, bring down the next group and repeat the process. In this case the next group is 00. Be sure to keep track of the decimal point.
Double your quotient as before and place it to the left of the new dividend.
Ignoring the last 0 in 2600, find out how many times 106 will go into 260. Place your result in the quotient and on the end of the 106.
Multiply the 1062 by 2 and place the result under the 2600 and then subtract.
Now you have the square root of 2835 at 53.2. 53.2 squared equals 2830.24, a lot closer to the original number 2835.
Repeating the process will give a closer answer. Ensure you follow how the new number in the answer was obtained.
Using a calculator gives an answer of 53.244718. The answer 53.24 is close and would be accepted.
